question.explanation:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

\begin{align*} -6\log_3{(x-3)} &= -24 \\[5pt] \log_3{(x-3)} &= \frac {-24}{-6} \\[5pt] \log_3{(x-3)} &= 4 \end{align*}

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $3,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

\begin{align*} \log_3{(x-3)} &=4\\[3pt] 3^{\color{blue}\log_3(x - 3)} &=3^{\color{blue}4} \end{align*}

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get $3^{\log_3 (x - 3)} = x - 3.$

Therefore, \begin{align*} x - 3 & = 3^4\\[3pt] x -3 & = 81\\[3pt] x & = 84. \end{align*}

question.text: If $7\log_5{x} - 2\log_5{x} = 10$, then what is the value of $x?$
question.explanation:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

\begin{align*} 7\log_5 x - 2\log_5 x &= 10 \\[3pt] (7-2)\log_5 x &= 10 \\[3pt] 5 \log_5 x &= 10 \\[3pt] \log_5 x &= 2 \end{align*}

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $5,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

\begin{align*} \log_5 x &= 2 \\[5pt] 5^{\color{blue}\log_5 x} &=5^{\color{blue}2} \end{align*}

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get $5^{\log_5 x} = x.$

Therefore, \begin{align*} x &= 5^{2} \\[3pt] x &= 25. \end{align*}
